reasons: Numeric warning signals (aggregate of R-series ratios; card gives no individual F/R IDs): 3 of 4 computable flags are triggered (from Beneish M > -1.78, Dechow F > 1.0, accruals > 3% of assets, OCF < 0.8x net income). Earnings that are this weak relative to cash, plus manipulation-model flags, are the strongest signal on the card.

Prior-period corrections and accounting changes (aggregate of F-series fields): 1 of 3 present. It may be a restatement/revision, which would be a direct sign of past misstatement, or only a segment change or voluntary accounting change. The card does not say which, so this raises risk only moderately.

Investigations and litigation (aggregate of F-series fields): 1 of 3 present (SEC, class action or other government). Any one of these raises concern, but a class action alone is common and often not specific.

Internal control and audit: 0 of 4 (no material weakness, adverse ICFR opinion, auditor change or disagreement). Management turnover: 0 of 2 (no CEO/CFO change or interim CFO). Both lower the risk a lot, because serious misstatements often come with control failures or executive departures.

Financial pressure 1 of 4 and transaction complexity 2 of 8 are at roughly typical levels for a large filer (e.g. incentive pay tied to EPS, over-time revenue or an acquisition). They add little extra risk.

Overall: strong numeric signals plus one correction or change flag and one investigation flag, against clean controls and stable management, give moderate risk. Because the card is aggregate-only, the score is held near the middle of the range.
